transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Tomás (Redwood SE), Liam (Rythmiq), Priya (Rythmiq), Noah (Rythmiq PM)
Shared links: Pilot doc (drive): https://drive.redwood/pilot/rythmiq, Benchmarks: https://redwood.app/pilot/rythmiq/benchmarks

Summary: quick sync to go over week 4 cache numbers, where hit-rate is, and what to tune next. Short checkpoints and assign owners.

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Liam (Rythmiq): Yep hear you.
[00:08] Priya (Rythmiq): All good.
[00:12] Aisha: Cool. Agenda: show the updated prefetch + eviction approach Tomás ran in the bench, discuss the real traffic numbers you sent, align on A/B steps and pricing, and schedule any infra deep dive.
[00:24] Tomás (Redwood): Hi all. I'll jump straight to the bench results. Reminder: we tested two modes — prefix-first prefetch and hybrid KV-prefetch with TTL-aware eviction. Synthetic trace used your 7-day sample but we jittered user IDs to avoid user bias.
[00:40] Tomás: Baseline (week 3 config) had avg KV hit 31% and p95 latency for generation path at 170ms on our rig. With the new hybrid prefetch we measured 48% KV hit and p95 down to ~115ms, CPU/GPU utilization remained comparable.
[01:05] Liam: Wait 48%? That's a big jump. Is that on synthetic or live reproduction?
[01:11] Tomás: Synthetic with your traffic profile; we also ran a small shadow on live traffic for 2 hours on a canary node — that saw ~42% hit. The difference is due to cold-starts and session fragmentation in live.
[01:25] Noah (Rythmiq): Can you explain hybrid prefetch a bit more? I'm not fully following the eviction piece.
[01:30] Tomás: Sure. Hybrid means we prefetch when prefix frequency exceeds a threshold but we also keep a KV TTL and an LRU-weighted eviction that penalizes large prefix footprints. So long, repeated prefixes stay hot, ephemeral ones age out faster. We also bias for prompt reuse where session-level prompts are recognized and pinned for that session window.
[01:55] Priya: That pinning — is it per-session memory? We're worried about memory blow-up when we have long conversational sessions.
[02:02] Tomás: Good call. Pinning is capped per-session (configurable, defaults to 4 prompts pinned). We observed very few sessions require more than 6 pins in your traces. If you expect multi-hour sessions we can lower the cap.
[02:18] Liam: Are the TTLs static or adaptive? Our users have a mix of short queries and multi-turn workflows.
[02:24] Tomás: Adaptive TTLs. TTL initial values come from empirical prefix frequency, then the system extends TTL on access. We also have an aggressive eviction mode for peak times to keep p95 latency bounded.
[02:40] Aisha: Real quick — we noticed you have a lot of near-duplicate prompts in the feed. Some are identical with token differences. Any chance you can share how dedupe is handled upstream?
[02:50] Priya: We do some lightweight fingerprinting but it's in the queue; it's not perfect. We wanted to see if Redwood's prefix hashing would help reduce duplicates at the cache layer.
[02:58] Tomás: Yes, we do 64-bit prefix hashing with optional fuzzy matching (small edit distance). That helps group near-duplicates and increases effective hit-rate. Note: fuzzy matching increases false positives if users do long paraphrases; we usually enable it only for short prefix lengths (<=64 tokens).
[03:20] Noah: Do you have any numbers on false positives or wrong completions because of fuzzy grouping?
[03:24] Tomás: In bench tests false positive rate was <1.2% when fuzzy enabled for prefixes <64 tokens. We logged a couple examples — usually cosmetic differences. We suggest conservative rollout: enable fuzzy on a subset of routes first.
[03:38] Liam: On the cost side, does prefetch add a lot of extra tokens? I'm conscious about token billing.
[03:44] Aisha: Good point. Prefetching does increase tokens to the model for the cached prefix work, but because we avoid repeated full-model generation we still see net token reduction per user. In our bench, token consumption per request dropped ~12% overall vs baseline, because many requests hit cache and skip heavy decode paths.
[04:02] Priya: That's promising. Do you have the bench spreadsheets?
[04:06] Tomás: Yes, uploaded to the pilot folder — see Benchmarks tab. There's per-route breakdown, the token delta column, and cost estimate with both hosted and dedicated assumptions.
[04:18] Liam: We looked at week 3 logs — our KV hit was hovering 28-33% during peak and dropped overnight to ~18%. What explains the nocturnal dip?
[04:28] Tomás: Likely session churn: active users at night differ so hot prefixes shift. We saw reclaim pressure in the cluster overnight when background jobs and nightly retraining bursts compete for GPU memory. Two mitigations: (1) set a lower eviction aggressiveness overnight or (2) allocate reserved cache slices for high-value prefixes (pin across cluster).
[04:48] Priya: Option 2 sounds heavy-weight. Is option 1 simpler?
[04:51] Tomás: Option 1 is simpler — it's a config toggle in the cluster autoscaler/ejection policy. We can schedule a 'low aggression' window for your timezone; that will maintain higher hit but slightly increase average memory pressure.
[05:05] Noah: How does this play with Dedicated vs Hosted? We're leaning towards hosted for speed-to-prod but considering dedicated later.
[05:12] Aisha: Hosted gives you faster rollout and Redwood manages the cluster heuristics. Dedicated gives you more predictable isolation and you control eviction aggressiveness at the allocation level. For the pilot we recommend hosted; if you hit consistent scale we can flip to Dedicated later.
[05:28] Liam: Ok. If we run the 24h staging A/B and our hit goes to >45% in the tuned variant, that's a strong signal. But what's the best way to validate that quality hasn't regressed due to fuzzy matching?
[05:40] Tomás: Add a small human review set — sample 500 completions from both variants and run automated QA metrics (semantic similarity, hallucination markers). We can also attach our evaluation harness if you want.
[05:52] Priya: Could you post the QA harness and the script to compute semantic similarity?
[05:56] Tomás: Will do, link in the pilot doc.
[06:00] Aisha: Quick question on instrumentation — what logs do you need from our side?
[06:04] Priya: We can give request/response pairs, token counts, latencies, and your mention of session ids is okay. We cannot share PII.
[06:12] Tomás: That's perfect. Request id, route id, prefix hash, and cache hit boolean are the main things we ingest. If you can also include the raw prompt fingerprint that's helpful.
[06:23] Liam: We'll sanitize PII and push last 7 days as Priya mentioned.
[06:26] Aisha: Great. Let's move to chart review. Tomás, can you talk through the two charts on slide 3?
[06:32] Tomás: Chart 1 shows daily KV hit trends, baseline vs hybrid; you can see the spike during peak with hybrid. Chart 2 is p95 latency over the same period; hybrid pulls tail down by ~45ms in our bench.
[06:44] Noah: There's a dip where hybrid p95 briefly increases — what's that anomaly?
[06:48] Tomás: That was when we resized cache memory mid-bench; transient evictions caused a spike. That suggests we should avoid mid-test reconfig when collecting A/B.
[06:58] Liam: Understood. Any gotchas about prompt reuse — we've been experimenting with deduping at edge vs letting cache handle it.
[07:06] Tomás: Edge dedupe helps reduce unnecessary requests. Combined approach is best: edge dedupe for obvious exact duplicates, and cache fuzzy matching for near-duplicates. We do see diminishing returns if both are too aggressive.
[07:20] Priya: For retries and timeouts — if cache misses, we fallback to generation; do you recommend any client-side retry logic?
[07:27] Tomás: Keep client-side retry conservative (single retry with exponential backoff). Server-side fallback is fast; client retries create duplicates and thrash the cache.
[07:36] Aisha: On the governance side, Noah had a question about data residency — we promised to check SSO/SSO logs earlier?
[07:42] Noah: Right — also audit logs for who touched cache configs. It's a compliance ask.
[07:47] Aisha: Redwood's console logs config changes; we can share an example audit export. We'll add that to the security pack.
[07:54] Liam: About pricing — will prefetch increase billable tokens for hosted? I know you said net reduction but want to see numbers.
[08:00] Aisha: We'll share the token delta table. For hosted, prefetch costs are included in the usage; we model both worst-case token increase and average token reduction. For Dedicated pricing, we show reserved capacity and an ops surcharge for advanced prefetching.
[08:14] Priya: Anything else from your bench on memory usage impact?
[08:18] Tomás: Prefetch increases memory footprint per node by ~6-10% depending on pin cap. But because we reduce decode trips, GPU time per request falls and net throughput improves.
[08:31] Noah: That helps. Next — A/B specifics. Liam, what exactly will you run on staging?
[08:36] Liam: We'll do a 4-hour A/B during a morning window, split traffic 50/50, and collect hit-rate, p95, and a small sample of completions for QA. Aim to run this by Monday.
[08:47] Aisha: Sounds good. We'll provide the exact config file to drop in your cluster. Tomás, you'll post the CLI to flip the rule set?
[08:53] Tomás: Yes, will post a small script and the prefetch policy JSON.
[08:57] Priya: If the A/B looks good, what is the recommended rollout size? Full rollout or gradual?
[09:02] Tomás: Gradual — 25% for 2 hours, then 50% for 6 hours, then full if metrics hold. Also enable canary alerts for p95 >120ms or hit-rate <40%.
[09:15] Liam: If we get hit-rate >45% on staging, is it fair to consider that a success metric for pilot?
[09:20] Aisha: Yes that's aligned with what we discussed — combine with QA pass and p95 <120ms. We'll add those to the sign-off doc.
[09:28] Noah: One more technical — how does model quantization interact with KV cache keys? We've seen slight logits shift after 4-bit quantization.
[09:36] Tomás: Cache keys are computed pre-quantization on normalized tokens, so quantization shouldn't affect keying. Where it matters is output similarity; quantized models can change generation probabilities so QA matters. We test across both FP16 and int4 in bench.
[09:52] Priya: Good to know.
[09:55] Aisha: Ok we're near time. Quick recap and owners.
[10:00] Aisha: Tomás to post prefetch JSON, CLI snippet, and QA harness (due 2026-11-14).
[10:06] Tomás: Yup.
[10:07] Aisha: Liam & Priya to run 4-hour staging A/B and upload logs (due 2026-11-16).
[10:12] Liam: On it.
[10:13] Aisha: I will share pilot pricing and SLA addendum (due 2026-11-15).
[10:16] Noah: We'll look for the docs and organize the infra deep-dive on 2026-11-20.
[10:20] Aisha: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the doc and set the calendar invite for the infra deep dive.
[10:25] Liam: Thanks.
[10:26] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: automated capture clipped some overlapping talk and mis-typed a few product nouns (e.g., "KVcash"). See action items for exact deliverables.
